Deterministic: polluter calls System.setProperty("odfixture.turbo", "true") and never clears it; victim asserts FeatureFlags.isTurboEnabled() is false. Victim passes alone and fails every time it runs after the polluter.

Victim fails only when both ToggleAPolluterTest#setFlagA and ToggleBPolluterTest#setFlagB have run before it; the relative order of A and B does not matter.

ADR-008 case (W-next): the polluter class name (ZzzLatePolluterTest) sorts alphabetically AFTER the victim class name (AlwaysEarlyVictimTest), and test discovery in this project is alphabetical by class (confirmed in docs/evidence-m2.md's W7 Task 3). So in the module's natural discovered order the victim always runs before the polluter, and the original-order repetition (ADR-008 step 1) can never reproduce the bug -- this case exists specifically to exercise ADR-008 step 2 (trying shuffled orders) and is not reproducible by the pre-ADR-008 pipeline at all. A shuffle that places ZzzLatePolluterTest#setLateFlag before AlwaysEarlyVictimTest#expectsLateFlagUnset must reproduce the failure deterministically: the polluter sets LateFlag.isSet = true and never restores it; the victim asserts LateFlag.isSet is false. The victim passes alone and in the natural (alphabetical) order; it fails only when the polluter precedes it, which requires reordering to discover.

CONFIRMED 2026-10-10 by Member 3, real runs (native Windows, JDK 24): real discovered order places AlwaysEarlyVictimTest first and ZzzLatePolluterTest last of 16 methods, confirming it is unreachable without reordering. Real diagnose() on the natural order (n=5): NOT_REPRODUCED, as designed -- this is expected, not a problem (the natural order genuinely never fails). Real one-fresh-JVM run with the explicit order [ZzzLatePolluterTest#setLateFlag, AlwaysEarlyVictimTest#expectsLateFlagUnset]: polluter passes, victim FAILS with java.lang.AssertionError at AlwaysEarlyVictimTest.expectsLateFlagUnset:15 -- matches the predicted mechanism exactly. Victim run alone: passes. Not yet confirmed through the full ADR-008 shuffle-search pipeline end to end (Member 2's step 4, not yet landed) -- that confirmation is real order-dependent behaviour, independently verified by hand; only the automated discovery of the right order remains pending.

Deliberately fails in isolation (assertEquals(2, 1) always fails). Any tool must report this as not order-dependent because it already fails with no polluter run first. Confirmed against the finalized Phase 3 decision table (eval/outcome.py): this maps to UNRESOLVED(VICTIM_FAILS_ALONE).

Fails intermittently, independent of any shared static field, system property, or execution order. Originally guessed NOT_REPRODUCED in Phase 1 (flagged there as pending confirmation). Resolved once the Phase 3 decision table was finalized: the isolation check observes the SAME failure signature recurring at least once even when run alone with no polluter present, which trips UNRESOLVED(VICTIM_FAILS_ALONE) before reproduction counting is ever consulted -- not NOT_REPRODUCED, since it does sometimes fail, just not because of any polluter. This is the correct category for any failure that recurs by itself, deterministically (N1) or intermittently (N2).

MECHANISM FIXED 2026-10-10: originally used System.nanoTime() % 2L == 0L, which inspects nanoTime()'s lowest bit. On a real machine (Windows 11, JDK 21) that bit was always 0 (the timer's resolution was a 100ns-granular, always-even value), so the test deterministically PASSED there -- 0/40 failures, both alone and in the full order -- the opposite of 'unrelated to the environment.' On the original Linux/JDK8 container the same mechanism gave a genuine ~55-60% failure rate (12/20 in one Phase-1 measurement), so the bug was real but environment-specific, not visible everywhere. Replaced with new java.util.Random().nextBoolean(), which mixes nanoTime() with a per-call atomic counter through a full LCG rather than exposing one raw timer bit. Re-verified for real on both environments after the fix: native Windows/JDK24 11/20 fail (45%), Docker Linux/JDK8 10/20 fail (50%) -- genuinely balanced on both, confirming the fix addresses the root cause rather than just moving the symptom. See docs/evidence-m3.md for the full investigation.

ADR-008 case (W-next): the real-world failure this models depends on an external environment variable (illustratively 'CI=true' in ADR-008's own text) that the original bug report's CI system set, but that FlakeTrace's own controlled re-execution never sets. We deliberately did NOT use the literal name 'CI' for the check, because GitHub Actions itself sets CI=true on every real runner -- using that exact name would make this negative control fail on our own CI job, which is the opposite of the point. The fixture instead checks a fictitious variable name (FLAKETRACE_N3_NEVER_SET) that nothing in this project's toolchain, Maven, or CI sets, while keeping the same shape ADR-008 describes: a victim whose real failure cause is outside anything FlakeTrace controls or observes. Expected: the victim passes every time under FlakeTrace (original order, every shuffled order ADR-008 tries, and alone), with no polluter ever blamed -- UNRESOLVED(NOT_REPRODUCED), honestly reporting that the given evidence never reproduced the originally-reported failure, not that the test is reliable.

CONFIRMED 2026-10-10 by Member 3, real diagnose() run (native Windows, JDK 24, n=5): status NOT_REPRODUCED, 0/5 reproduced in the natural order, no polluter blamed, reference_signature None (it really never failed) -- exactly as designed. Not yet confirmed as a full schema-validated UNRESOLVED(NOT_REPRODUCED) report end to end: today's diagnose() stops before running the victim-alone check when nothing reproduces at all, so alone_n is 0, which eval.outcome.DecisionInput rejects (isolation_n must be > 0) -- the exact gap ADR-008 names. That confirmation is pending Member 2's diagnose() change (always run the alone check), tracked as ADR-008 step 4; Member 3's own schema/decide()/assemble_report side (step 3) is independent of it and tested with hand-built DiagnosisRuns objects in the meantime, per this project's established testing convention.
